checklist.notes: The word ‘tool’ in the speaking instruction inherits the text-to-speech tool named in the same paragraph, obscuring the distinct listening capability required.
The four timed stages and one minimal-pair contrast are appropriately bounded for 35 minutes.
The final success condition requires independent identification, but one stated route cannot perform that task, weakening the practice-to-verification chain.
The repair dialogue and role switching enact basic participation around a safe personal fact.
Articulation practice precedes a repair model, attempted independent checking, and a short role-play.
The speaking check tells the learner to ask a helper or the previously named text-to-speech tool what it heard, but text-to-speech cannot listen to or identify the learner’s production.
Visible mouth-shape guidance and permission to mark an unavailable check are supportive without population-wide assumptions.

methods: Inspected only the supplied audit provenance declarations and project-authored snapshot-bound context; no external comparison was performed.

findings.description: The required independent speaking check offers a text-to-speech tool as though it could hear and identify live/leave. A TTS system produces speech rather than recognizing the learner’s speech, so the named self-study route cannot establish the success criterion.
findings.recommendation: Name a genuinely listening-capable route such as an independent human listener or explicitly suitable speech-recognition tool, distinguish it from TTS, and retain ‘not checked’ when neither is available.
